title: Remove the remaining limits on shop trading hours
action: Let retailers choose their own opening hours, keeping any restrictions only for Christmas Day, Good Friday and the morning of Anzac Day, applied to all retailers alike; separate rules for alcohol and gambling can stay.
why: Online shops never close, so trading-hours limits mainly handicap physical stores and favour some formats over others; deregulation where it has happened widened choice.

evidence.source: Competition Policy Review: Final Report (Harper review)
evidence.quote: Remaining restrictions on retail trading hours should be removed. To the extent that jurisdictions choose to retain restrictions, these should be strictly limited to Christmas Day, Good Friday and the morning of ANZAC Day, and should be applied broadly to avoid discriminating among different types of retailers.

tradeoffs: Penalty rates and staff preferences are set through workplace law, not trading-hours rules.
